quests.question: She checked her phone repeatedly ____ she finally got a reply.
quests.sentence: She checked her phone repeatedly ____ she finally got a reply.
quests.hint: Checking continued right up to the moment the reply arrived.
quests.explanation: 'Until' marks the endpoint of a repeated action. She kept checking UNTIL the reply came - at that point, the repeated checking stopped. 'When' describes a single moment, not the ongoing duration.

quests.question: He felt much more relaxed ____ he had taken a proper holiday.
quests.sentence: He felt much more relaxed ____ he had taken a proper holiday.
quests.hint: The holiday came first; the relaxation followed as a result.
quests.explanation: 'After' shows sequence. He took a holiday (earlier event) and felt more relaxed afterwards (later state). 'Because' would also work logically, but 'after' focuses on the time sequence.

quests.question: She brought a light jacket ____ the evenings tend to get cool there.
quests.sentence: She brought a light jacket ____ the evenings tend to get cool there.
quests.hint: Knowing that evenings get cool is the reason she brought the jacket.
quests.explanation: 'Because' gives the practical reason for a precautionary action. Cool evenings (reason) explain bringing a jacket (action). This is a clear, direct cause-and-effect.

quests.question: The food was a little disappointing ____ the restaurant's atmosphere was wonderful.
quests.sentence: The food was a little disappointing ____ the restaurant's atmosphere was wonderful.
quests.hint: Disappointing food and a wonderful atmosphere seem to contradict each other.
quests.explanation: 'Although' introduces a concession. The disappointing food (negative aspect) is contrasted with the wonderful atmosphere (positive aspect) - 'although' shows both exist simultaneously, with the positive being the main point.

quests.question: She always waves enthusiastically at the camera ____ she spots one.
quests.sentence: She always waves enthusiastically at the camera ____ she spots one.
quests.hint: Spotting a camera is the regular trigger for waving.
quests.explanation: 'When' connects a habitual trigger (spotting a camera) to a habitual response (waving). This happens every time - 'while' would suggest she waves throughout an extended period of spotting.

quests.question: He has been much more careful with money ____ he lost his job last year.
quests.sentence: He has been much more careful with money ____ he lost his job last year.
quests.hint: Losing his job was the turning point - he has been careful from that moment to now.
quests.explanation: 'Since' marks the starting point of a continuing behavioural change. He has been careful (present perfect) SINCE he lost his job (specific past event). The present perfect + 'since' is the standard structure for this meaning.

quests.question: He tended to his vegetable garden ____ his wife cooked lunch inside.
quests.sentence: He tended to his vegetable garden ____ his wife cooked lunch inside.
quests.hint: Both activities happened at the same time, one outside and one inside the house.
quests.explanation: 'While' connects two simultaneous activities happening in different places. He worked in the garden (his activity) at the same time his wife cooked lunch indoors (her activity) - both happened together during the same part of the day.

quests.question: Always read the terms and conditions carefully ____ you sign anything.
quests.sentence: Always read the terms and conditions carefully ____ you sign anything.
quests.hint: Reading must come first - before signing, not after.
quests.explanation: 'Before' shows the necessary prior action. You should read the terms BEFORE signing - once you have signed, it is too late to reconsider. The order matters here.

quests.question: She enjoyed the concert ____ she wasn't at all familiar with the music.
quests.sentence: She enjoyed the concert ____ she wasn't at all familiar with the music.
quests.hint: Enjoying unfamiliar music is a pleasant and unexpected discovery.
quests.explanation: 'Though' (informal for 'although') introduces a concession. Being unfamiliar with the music (concessive fact) would normally reduce enjoyment, but she enjoyed it - 'though' shows the expected outcome did not happen.

quests.question: They celebrated with a meal out ____ they received the fantastic news.
quests.sentence: They celebrated with a meal out ____ they received the fantastic news.
quests.hint: The news came first; the celebration followed.
quests.explanation: 'After' shows chronological sequence. Receiving the news (earlier event) led to celebrating with a meal (later action). 'When' could also work, but 'after' emphasises that the news came first.

quests.question: He decided to take a taxi ____ he was already running behind schedule.
quests.sentence: He decided to take a taxi ____ he was already running behind schedule.
quests.hint: Running late is the direct reason for choosing a taxi.
quests.explanation: 'Because' gives the direct, practical reason for a decision. Being late (reason) explains choosing a taxi (action). 'So' would also work but would require the clauses to be reversed.

quests.question: She always feels a little nervous ____ she meets someone new for the first time.
quests.sentence: She always feels a little nervous ____ she meets someone new for the first time.
quests.hint: Meeting someone new is the regular social trigger for feeling nervous.
quests.explanation: 'When' connects a regular trigger (meeting someone new) to a habitual emotional response (feeling nervous). This happens every time - 'before' would suggest she feels nervous before the actual meeting.

quests.question: The company has grown considerably ____ it launched its online store.
quests.sentence: The company has grown considerably ____ it launched its online store.
quests.hint: The online store launch was the starting point of the company's growth.
quests.explanation: 'Since' marks the starting point of a continuing trend. The company has grown (present perfect) FROM the time of the launch (specific past event) TO the present. The present perfect + 'since' is the correct structure.

quests.question: ____ the journey took far longer than planned, everyone arrived safely in the end.
quests.sentence: ____ the journey took far longer than planned, everyone arrived safely in the end.
quests.hint: A long journey is a drawback - but everyone arriving safely is the positive outcome.
quests.explanation: 'Although' at the start introduces a concessive fact. The long journey (negative aspect) is acknowledged, but the safe arrival (positive outcome) is the main point - 'although' shows the negative did not prevent the positive.

quests.question: She drafted her reply ____ she was still in the morning meeting.
quests.sentence: She drafted her reply ____ she was still in the morning meeting.
quests.hint: Drafting and being in the meeting were simultaneous activities.
quests.explanation: 'While' connects two simultaneous activities. She was drafting a reply (background task) during the same time she was supposed to be in the meeting (foreground obligation). Both happened at the same time.

quests.question: He kept revising his essay ____ he was completely satisfied with it.
quests.sentence: He kept revising his essay ____ he was completely satisfied with it.
quests.hint: Revising continued right up to the moment of complete satisfaction.
quests.explanation: 'Until' marks the endpoint of a repeated effort. He kept revising UNTIL he was happy with the result (the stopping condition). The revision process lasted as long as necessary to reach that standard.

quests.question: She accepted the invitation to speak ____ she had very little free time.
quests.sentence: She accepted the invitation to speak ____ she had very little free time.
quests.hint: Accepting when you have no time is a generous but surprising decision.
quests.explanation: 'Though' introduces a concessive contrast. Having little free time (obstacle) would normally prevent accepting such an invitation, but she accepted anyway - 'though' highlights that she overcame the constraint.

quests.question: He called his family straight away ____ he landed at the airport.
quests.sentence: He called his family straight away ____ he landed at the airport.
quests.hint: Landing came first; calling followed immediately afterwards.
quests.explanation: 'After' shows the sequence. He landed (earlier event) and then called his family (immediate subsequent action). 'When' could also work, but 'after' specifically emphasises that he waited until he had landed.

quests.question: They switched off the television ____ they wanted to focus on their conversation.
quests.sentence: They switched off the television ____ they wanted to focus on their conversation.
quests.hint: Wanting to focus is the deliberate reason for switching off the TV.
quests.explanation: 'Because' gives the deliberate, conscious reason for an action. Wanting to focus (reason) explains switching off the TV (action). This is a purposeful choice made for a clear stated reason.

quests.question: The dog always barks ____ the postman pushes letters through the door.
quests.sentence: The dog always barks ____ the postman pushes letters through the door.
quests.hint: The postman's action is the regular trigger for barking.
quests.explanation: 'When' connects a habitual trigger (postman pushing letters) to a habitual response (barking). This happens every time - 'while' would suggest ongoing barking throughout an extended postal delivery.

quests.question: She hasn't left the house much ____ she had her back operation two weeks ago.
quests.sentence: She hasn't left the house much ____ she had her back operation two weeks ago.
quests.hint: The operation was the turning point - she has barely left home since then.
quests.explanation: 'Since' marks the starting point of an ongoing change in behaviour. She hasn't been going out (present perfect negative) SINCE her operation (specific past event). The present perfect + 'since' shows this has continued from then to now.

quests.question: ____ it was a Monday morning, the high street was surprisingly busy.
quests.sentence: ____ it was a Monday morning, the high street was surprisingly busy.
quests.hint: A Monday morning would normally be quiet - a busy high street is unexpected.
quests.explanation: 'Although' at the start introduces a concessive fact. Monday mornings are usually quiet (expected), but the high street was busy (unexpected outcome) - 'although' captures this surprising contrast.

quests.question: He grew more and more confident ____ he settled into his new role at work.
quests.sentence: He grew more and more confident ____ he settled into his new role at work.
quests.hint: Confidence developed gradually in proportion to settling into the role.
quests.explanation: 'As' expresses parallel, proportional development. His confidence grew at the same rate as he settled in - both changed together over time. This is the gradual-change use of 'as'.

quests.question: She always prepares her key points mentally ____ she walks into a job interview.
quests.sentence: She always prepares her key points mentally ____ she walks into a job interview.
quests.hint: Mental preparation must come before entering - not after.
quests.explanation: 'Before' shows prior action. She prepares BEFORE walking in - mental preparation needs to happen before the interview starts. 'When' would suggest she prepares at the moment of walking in, which is too late.

quests.question: She automatically reaches for her phone ____ she hears a notification sound.
quests.sentence: She automatically reaches for her phone ____ she hears a notification sound.
quests.hint: A notification sound is the immediate trigger for reaching for the phone.
quests.explanation: 'When' marks the specific trigger that causes an automatic response. The sound (trigger) causes the hand movement (response) - this is a habitual, almost reflexive reaction. 'While' would suggest extended reaching.

quests.question: ____ she tried several times, she couldn't quite crack the soufflé recipe.
quests.sentence: ____ she tried several times, she couldn't quite crack the soufflé recipe.
quests.hint: Multiple attempts are acknowledged - but the result was still failure.
quests.explanation: 'Though' at the start of a sentence introduces the concessive clause first. Several attempts (positive effort) would normally lead to success, but she still couldn't do it - 'though' shows the effort did not produce the expected result.

quests.question: They kept searching the whole house ____ they found the missing car keys.
quests.sentence: They kept searching the whole house ____ they found the missing car keys.
quests.hint: Searching continued right up to the moment of finding the keys.
quests.explanation: 'Until' marks the endpoint of a continuous action. They searched UNTIL the keys were found (the stopping point). At that moment, the search ended.

quests.question: She has been playing the violin ____ she was six years old.
quests.sentence: She has been playing the violin ____ she was six years old.
quests.hint: Age six was the starting point - she has played from then to now.
quests.explanation: 'Since' with the present perfect ('has been playing') shows a skill that began at a specific age (six) and has continued to the present. This is a classic 'since + age/time' structure.

quests.question: He took a long walk to clear his head ____ he had an argument with his brother.
quests.sentence: He took a long walk to clear his head ____ he had an argument with his brother.
quests.hint: The argument happened first; the walk to recover came afterwards.
quests.explanation: 'After' shows the chronological sequence. The argument (earlier stressful event) led to the walk (subsequent coping action). He walked to clear his head AFTER the argument.

quests.question: She keeps a spare key at her neighbour's house ____ she sometimes locks herself out.
quests.sentence: She keeps a spare key at her neighbour's house ____ she sometimes locks herself out.
quests.hint: Occasionally locking herself out is the practical reason for the spare key.
quests.explanation: 'Because' gives the practical, precautionary reason for an action. The risk of locking herself out (reason) explains keeping a spare key with the neighbour (precaution). This is a clear cause-driven habit.
